Yeah, I had to reread the story a few times to try and get any sense of a timeline. There are a number of holes in the story.

The intruder had a gun when he started downstairs. Where was that gun when the kid went to get the 9mm, or when he drew in on the intruder?

When the man reappeared moments later, the boy told WVTM-TV, the individual was holding a gun. “When he was coming down the stairs, that’s when he told me he was going to kill me, f-you and all that,” Chris said. Instead of running, Chris told the station, he upgraded his weaponry, picking up a 9mm handgun that was in the home.

I'll give the fact that I don't know the layout of the home, and that the kid could have moved away from the stairs (potentially a stairwell instead of a more open staircase) as the kid being able to move out of sight from the intruder to grab the gun. But once the kid confronts the intruder with the 9mm, the kid says that the intruder didn't think it was real. Again, what happened to the gun the intruder had?

“I guess when I pulled the gun out on him he didn’t think it was a real gun cause he didn’t worry about it,” Chris told the station. “He just kept on walking.”

And then next it reads that the intruder is walking out of the home with a stolen laundry hamper.

So the intruder, who had reportedly been threatening to kill the kid, had a gun, and then ignored the 9mm drawn on him, ends up grabbing an item from the house while the 9mm is drawn on him before walking out of the house. There's a lot of holes there that make this a bit fishy to read - whether it's due to the kid's story or just poor reporting.
